summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and prostate cancer undergoing radiation therapy, was admitted for urinary retention and a complicated urinary tract infection caused by ESBL-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. He had a similar episode three weeks prior with a Foley catheter and infection. This admission was marked by acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration, which improved with cautious IV hydration. He developed C. difficile colitis secondary to ciprofloxacin, requiring oral vancomycin. His medications were adjusted: tacrolimus was increased due to subtherapeutic levels, doxazosin was added for urinary retention, and carvedilol was reduced to mitigate hypotensive risk. His symptoms resolved, kidney function returned to baseline, and he was discharged home with a plan to complete antibiotic courses, restart lisinopril after PCP evaluation, and follow up with his transplant and oncology teams.
